title: Hardening an SSH server
summary: Verify a server's identity, switch to key-based login, then turn off password and root logins.

nodes.server: a new Linux server, 10.20.1.10, user dev

tasks.title: Is this really the server?
tasks.text: The first time you SSH somewhere, the client shows the server's host key fingerprint and asks if you trust it. Check it out of band: on **server** itself, find the SHA256 fingerprint of its **ED25519** host key. Submit it (it starts with `SHA256:`).

solution.note: Now compare it with what `ssh dev@10.20.1.10` shows on the workstation before typing yes. If they ever differ, someone may be intercepting the connection.

tasks.title: Log in with a key
tasks.text: The account `dev` currently logs in with the password `{{PASS}}`. On **workstation**, create an SSH key pair and install the public key for `dev` on the server, so that key login works without any password prompt.

checks.cmd: ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=4 dev@10.20.1.10 true
checks.fail_msg: Key-based login as dev from workstation does not work yet.

hints: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519` creates `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` (private, never share) and `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` (public). Press Enter to accept defaults.
`ssh-copy-id dev@10.20.1.10` appends your public key to the server's `/home/dev/.ssh/authorized_keys`, using the password once.

steps.cmd: ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -f /root/.ssh/id_ed25519 && sshpass -p '{{PASS}}' ssh-copy-id -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -i /root/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub dev@10.20.1.10 >/dev/null 2>&1

tasks.title: Turn off passwords
tasks.text: Passwords can be guessed (remember lab 9); keys realistically cannot. On **server**, disable password authentication in the SSH daemon and reload it. Your key login must keep working.

checks.cmd: sshpass -p '{{PASS}}' ssh -o PubkeyAuthentication=no -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=4 dev@10.20.1.10 true
checks.fail_msg: The server still accepts the password.

checks.cmd: ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=4 dev@10.20.1.10 true

hints: The daemon's settings are in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config`. Look for `PasswordAuthentication`.
Set it to `PasswordAuthentication no`, check the file with `sshd -t` (no output means OK), then reload: `kill -HUP $(cat /run/sshd.pid)`.
Keep your existing session open while you change SSH settings on a real server. If the new config locks you out, that session is your way back in.

tasks.title: No direct root login
tasks.text: Admins should log in as themselves and use `sudo`, so every action is tied to a person. On **server**, forbid root logins over SSH entirely and reload the daemon.

checks.fail_msg: PermitRootLogin is not set to no.

checks.cmd: ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=4 dev@10.20.1.10 true
checks.fail_msg: Key login as dev stopped working.

hints: `sshd -T` prints the effective configuration: `sshd -T | grep -i permitroot`.
